content: 1. The combination of testosterone buccal system and pretomanid can increase the toxicity of one another. This interaction is classified as serious, and it is recommended to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. Pretomanid is associated with hepatotoxicity, so alcohol and hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements and drugs other than bedaquiline and linezolid, should be avoided. 2. The combination of testosterone intranasal and pretomanid also increases the toxicity of one another. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be considered. Pretomanid's hepatotoxicity necessitates avoiding alcohol and hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements and drugs other than bedaquiline and linezolid. 3. The combination of testosterone topical and pretomanid similarly increases mutual toxicity. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Pretomanid's hepatotoxicity requires avoiding alcohol and hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements and drugs other than bedaquiline and linezolid. 4. The combination of thioguanine and pretomanid increases the toxicity of one another. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Pretomanid's hepatotoxicity necessitates avoiding alcohol and hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements and drugs other than bedaquiline and linezolid. 5. The combination of ticlopidine and pretomanid increases the toxicity of one another. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Pretomanid's hepatotoxicity requires avoiding alcohol and hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements and drugs other than bedaquiline and linezolid. 6. The combination of valproic acid and pretomanid increases the toxicity of one another. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Pretomanid's hepatotoxicity necessitates avoiding alcohol and hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements and drugs other than bedaquiline and linezolid. 7. Pretomanid increases the level or effect of valsartan through other mechanisms. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. Increased monitoring for drug-related adverse effects is recommended when pretomanid is coadministered with sensitive OATP1B3 substrates. 8. Pretomanid increases the level or effect of verapamil through other mechanisms. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. Increased monitoring for drug-related adverse effects is recommended when pretomanid is coadministered with sensitive P-gp substrates. 9. The combination of vitamin A and pretomanid increases the toxicity of one another. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Pretomanid's hepatotoxicity necessitates avoiding alcohol and hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements and drugs other than bedaquiline and linezolid. 10. The combination of vitamin D and pretomanid increases the toxicity of one another. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Pretomanid's hepatotoxicity requires avoiding alcohol and hepatotoxic agents, including herbal supplements and drugs other than bedaquiline and linezolid. 11. Pretomanid increases the level or effect of voxilaprevir through other mechanisms. Caution is advised, and close monitoring is required. Increased monitoring for drug-related adverse effects is recommended when pretomanid is coadministered with sensitive OATP1B3 substrates. 12. Pretomanid increases the level or effect of zidovudine through other mechanisms. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. In vitro studies have shown that pretomanid significantly inhibits OAT3, so monitoring for increased adverse effects and considering dosage reduction for OAT3 substrates is advised. 13. Pretomanid, when used in combination with bedaquiline and linezolid, has been associated with a high incidence of adverse effects, including peripheral neuropathy (81%), acne (39%), anemia (37%), nausea (37%), vomiting (34%), musculoskeletal pain (29%), headache (28%), increased transaminases (28%), dyspepsia (24%), decreased appetite (22%), rash (21%), pruritus (20%), abdominal pain (19%), pleuritic pain (19%), increased GGT (17%), lower respiratory tract infection (15%), hyperamylasemia (14%), hemoptysis (13%), cough (12%), visual impairment (12%), hypoglycemia (11%), abnormal weight loss (10%), diarrhea (10%), constipation (8%), gastritis (8%), neutropenia (8%), dry skin (7%), hypertension (7%), prolonged QT on ECG (6%), hyperlipasemia (6%), insomnia (6%), and thrombocytopenia (6%). 14. Pretomanid is contraindicated in patients for whom bedaquiline and/or linezolid are contraindicated. Hepatic adverse reactions have been reported with the combination, and treatment interruption may be necessary. Baseline and periodic monitoring of ALT, AST, alkaline phosphatase, and bilirubin levels are recommended. 15. Myelosuppression has been reported with the combination, a known adverse effect of linezolid. Consider reducing or interrupting linezolid dosing if myelosuppression worsens. 16. Peripheral and optic neuropathy have been reported, which are known adverse effects of linezolid. Interrupt linezolid if necessary. 17. QT prolongation has been reported with the combination, although pretomanid itself did not demonstrate QTc prolongation in cardiac electrophysiology testing. Discontinue treatment if clinically significant ventricular arrhythmia or a QTcF interval greater than 500 ms develops. If syncope occurs, obtain an ECG to detect QT prolongation. 18. Pretomanid caused testicular atrophy and impaired fertility in male rats. The effects on human male fertility have not been fully evaluated. 19. Lactic acidosis has been reported with the combination, a known adverse effect of linezolid. If recurrent nausea or vomiting occurs, immediately evaluate the patient, including bicarbonate and lactic acid levels. Consider interrupting linezolid dosing or the entire combination therapy. 20. No data are available on the use of pretomanid in pregnant women. No data are available regarding the presence of pretomanid in human milk, its effects on milk production, or its effects on the breastfed infant. However, it has been detected in rat milk. Because of the potential for adverse reactions in nursing infants, the benefits of breastfeeding should be weighed against the mother’s clinical need for the drug and any potential adverse effects on the infant. 21. Pretomanid is metabolized by multiple reductive and oxidative pathways, with no single pathway being predominant. In vitro studies using recombinant CYP3A4 demonstrated that this enzyme is responsible for approximately 20% of pretomanid metabolism. 22. Pretomanid must be taken with food. The tablet should be swallowed whole with water. It must only be used in combination with bedaquiline and linezolid as part of the recommended dosing regimen. Emphasize the importance of compliance with the full course of therapy to patients. Administer the combination regimen under directly observed therapy. 23. Pretomanid should be stored at room temperature, below 86°F (30°C).
